audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Vayne Levels 2, 3, first item and the two-item stage with 'Skill' on the rest, on the strength of prose claiming Maokai's root is dodgeable and his kit is 'CC-only'.
audit.why: The mirror audit (maokai__vayne) settled Levels 2 through First item to Maokai, with the two-item stage staying Vayne. The kit backs that: Twisted Advance is a lock-on dash that makes him untargetable and roots on arrival, Bramble Smash knocks back and grounds every 7s, and Sapling Toss zones from 1100. None of those is dodged by good spacing — they are all answered by cooldown tracking, which is what the lane actually is until Vayne's second item.
audit.corrected: phases[1..5].side and win[1..5] set to Maokai as matched pairs in one atomic group; Level 1 left as-is (the mirror did not state it) and 2+ items left as Vayne. whys[1] through whys[5] rewritten so the prose stops arguing the opposite.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text contained a raw authoring artefact — 'Sapling Toss (W... his E) poke' — shipped to the page, and no cooldown appeared anywhere.
audit.why: Sapling Toss is E, 1100 range on 18s at rank 1, and Riot's text notes it is more effective in brush. Twisted Advance is 14s at rank 1 falling to 10s at 525. Bramble Smash is 7s falling to 5s. Nature's Grasp is 130s at rank 1 with 3000 range. Those numbers turn 'play around his cooldowns' into something a player can actually count.
audit.corrected: spikes[0], spikes[1], early, mid, whys[2..5], dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns all carry real numbers now.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five strings tell you to dodge or sidestep Twisted Advance, and nothing mentions that Condemn shuts it off, that he goes untargetable during it, or that Bramble Smash grounds.
audit.why: Riot's text is explicit that Maokai 'contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target'. It is a lock-on: sidestepping does nothing, spending burst into it is wasted because he cannot be hit, and the actual answer is Condemn's knockback denying the dash. Bramble Smash grounds as well as knocking back, which is what strips Vayne's escape — and Vayne has no dash, so Nature's Grasp's advancing wall is a genuine retreat-cutter.
audit.corrected: early, mid, whys[1], wants.you[0], dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns rewritten around the untargetable lock-on, the Condemn denial, Bramble Smash's grounding and holding Flash for the wall.

audit.why: Sap Magic heals him on attack and its cooldown drops every time he casts or is hit by a spell, so it refreshes constantly in an extended trade. report[8].t already buys Executioner's Calling early; whys[5] now states the reason.

edits.before: Maokai is a slow, low-mobility tank whose only lane pressure is Sapling Toss (W... his E) poke and the Twisted Advance (W) root. Sidestep the sapling line, don't stand in brush he's warded, and Silver Bolts eats his HP whenever he walks up to last-hit.
edits.after: Sapling Toss (E) is his poke: 1100 range on an 18s cooldown, and Riot's text says it is more effective in brush, so stop fighting in it. Bramble Smash (Q) knocks you back every 7s and grounds you — that is the ability that ends your escape.

edits.before: Nature's Grasp (R) is a wide telegraphed root wave — dodge it with Tumble and he has zero follow-up burst. His entire kit is CC for a jungler to convert, so play around his cooldowns and he can't 1v1 you.
edits.after: Nature's Grasp (R) advances 3000 units on 130s at rank 1 and roots everything in its path — you have no dash, so hold Flash for the wall, not for the damage. His whole kit exists to set up a jungler.

notes: CHART CAVEAT: this packet reports Vayne on all seven rows over 509 games at 50.49%, which is not what the mirror settled. I followed the mirror as instructed and rewrote the prose to match, so the page is now internally consistent either way — but a 50.49% matchup where the enemy owns five of seven stages is worth a second look. UNVERIFIED, left alone: Nature's Grasp carries a terrain flag, which raises whether Condemn can slam Maokai into his own bramble wall for the stun. The kits do not settle whether that wall counts as terrain for Condemn's collision, so I wrote nothing about it — the mirror agent reached the same conclusion.
